intro.heading: Fit-Out Work Moves Fast. Untracked Scope Changes Move Faster.
intro.body: Interior work is not just bricks and cement, it is finishes, fixtures, and constant client change requests. Without a system that logs scope changes, matches vendor bills to delivery, and keeps approvals in one place, a healthy quote turns into a thin margin by handover.

personas.title: Scope Creep Eroding Margins With No Change-Order Tracking
personas.body: Clients ask for one more finish change, one more fixture swap. Without a logged, priced change order for each request, the extra cost is absorbed silently and the margin shrinks with every approval.

personas.title: Vendor Bills Paid Without Matching Delivery or Progress
personas.body: Furniture, fixtures, and fabric vendors invoice against a purchase order, but without checking what was actually delivered against what was ordered, short deliveries and price mismatches go through unnoticed.

personas.title: Client Approval Cycles Scattered Across WhatsApp Threads
personas.body: Design sign-offs, finish selections, and change requests get approved in chat messages that are impossible to search later. When a dispute comes up, there is no single record of what the client actually agreed to.

personas.title: Materials Ordered Without a Delivery Timeline Tied to the Schedule
personas.body: Furniture and fixtures get ordered on a call with no tracked delivery date. When the item arrives late, the carpentry team is already idle waiting for it, and the handover date slips.

personas.title: Retention and Warranty Papers Go Missing at Handover
personas.body: By the time a project reaches handover, retention amounts and warranty documents are scattered across emails and physical files, making the final close-out slower than it needs to be.

features.title: Plan and Schedule Every Stage Clearly
features.body: Design, procurement, execution, and handover are laid out as a single schedule. Tasks are assigned to the team and tracked as they are completed, not reported after the fact.
bullets: Design, purchase, and execution stages tracked as one timeline
Task assignment and completion visible in real time

features.title: Track Materials From Order to Site
features.body: Furniture, fixtures, and fabrics are tracked from purchase request through delivery, so the team always knows what has been ordered, what has arrived, and what is still pending before the next task can start.
bullets: Purchase requests and vendor delivery tracked in one view
Site execution never stalls waiting on an unclear order status

features.title: Match Vendor Bills to Delivery Before Payment
features.body: Vendor invoices are checked against what was actually delivered and installed, so a short delivery or a price mismatch is caught before the bill is approved, not after.
bullets: Vendor bills verified against delivered quantity, not the PO alone
Every billable change order tracked against the client budget

features.title: Keep Client Approvals in One Place
features.body: Design changes, finish selections, and client sign-offs are logged in SiteFlow instead of scattered across chat threads and email, so everyone works from the same approved record.
bullets: Every approval logged with date, item, and requester
Retention and warranty documents stored and searchable at handover

faqs.q: How does SiteFlow stop scope creep from eroding project margins?
faqs.a: Every client change request is logged as a priced change order before it is actioned, so the cost of a finish swap or an added fixture is visible against the budget immediately instead of being absorbed silently.

faqs.q: Can SiteFlow help manage client approvals instead of WhatsApp threads?
faqs.a: Yes. Design sign-offs, finish selections, and change requests are logged in one record with date and requester, so there is a single searchable trail instead of scattered chat messages.

faqs.q: Does SiteFlow check vendor bills against what was actually delivered?
faqs.a: Yes. Vendor invoices are matched against delivered and installed quantities before approval, so short deliveries or price mismatches are caught before payment, not after.

faqs.q: Is SiteFlow practical for a small interior firm with just a few active projects?
faqs.a: Yes. Interior firms typically start with quotations, scope tracking, vendor billing, and client invoicing, and expand into more modules as the number of active projects grows.
